name: Bosch Ltd
title: Bosch Ltd - 500530 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Bosch Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% y/y to INR58,419m and EBITDA to INR8,180m with margin near 14%, but management gave no capacity, utilisation or numeric guidance; supply-side evidence is absent.

summary.headline: Bosch Ltd Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR58,419 million and EBITDA rose 28% to INR8,180 million, with EBITDA margin near 14%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR58,419 million, up 22% YoY and 5% QoQ, led by Power Solutions and 2-wheeler Powersports. EBITDA was INR8,180 million (up 28% YoY, 4.7% QoQ), and management attributed the margin gain to revenue growth and expense optimisation. Reported PAT of INR7,018 million fell 37.1% YoY because the prior year included an exceptional gain on sale of video solutions and access/intrusion businesses; excluding it, PAT grew 9.9%. Management said the Chassis Systems acquisition was completed in July and consolidation starts this quarter.

financial_highlights.change: -37.1% YoY reported (prior year had exceptional gain); +9.9% YoY excluding exceptional; +23.4% QoQ

segments.name: Power Solutions
segments.commentary: Grew 29% YoY, outperforming the broader auto market across passenger cars, commercial vehicles, off-highway and tractors; management attributed this mainly to volume and recent new introductions.

segments.name: Mobility Aftermarket
segments.commentary: Grew 9.6% YoY and 8.7% QoQ, driven by lubricants, batteries, spark plugs and braking systems; independent aftermarket recorded its highest-ever monthly sales in June.

segments.name: 2-wheeler and Powersports
segments.commentary: Grew 41.4% YoY on value-added EMS products and premium motorcycle platforms; management said it gained market share and reported zero production disruptions.

segments.name: Consumer goods (Power Tools)
segments.commentary: Grew 20.9% YoY on tool demand and marketing campaigns, but declined 15.7% QoQ on seasonal factors.

guidance_outlook: Management expects 2-wheeler industry growth of about 8% next quarter, supported by festive demand, rural cash flows and infrastructure activity.
CAFE Phase 3 norms from April 2027 are expected to boost Power Solutions further; CV ADAS regulation starts October 2027.
Management said product mix should stay favourable through FY27 and that margin upward trend will be sustained, though it gave no numeric guidance.
Revenue from the e-axles JV with TACO is expected by late next year; JV order-book details to be shared in about a quarter.
Chassis Systems consolidated results start next quarter; FY26 segment sales breakup promised for the next call.
capex_capacity: Chassis Systems acquisition from a Bosch sister company was completed in July 2026; management sees minimal cost and synergy benefit and treats it as a powertrain-agnostic addition.
Management said no goodwill or amortisation arises from the Chassis acquisition.
JV with TACO (e-axles) to operate out of Nashik; JV with TSF Group (air systems) to operate out of Chennai; both still awaiting merger control clearances.
Investor meet planned at Chassis Systems plant in Chakan, Pune, in November 2026.
Localisation content is rising; management did not quantify the imports-from-parent share, which the annual report shows at about 53% of purchased goods.
demand_pricing: Passenger vehicle demand strong on SUV preference; HCV demand healthy despite a INR7.5 per litre diesel price increase; LCV and 3-wheeler demand robust; tractor demand resilient despite uneven monsoon.
Bosch said it outperformed market volume growth by a few percentage points.
Aftermarket turnaround attributed to strategic price positioning, new schemes, workshop programme expansion and launches such as Tulix LED lights, Prithvi HCV battery, and PC clutches and suspension.
Commodity prices rose sharply over recent quarters and have levelled off; management declined to give outlook.
Margin drivers cited: operational excellence, localisation, volume growth, productivity and favourable mix, with worldwide purchasing helping manage sourcing volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Is the aftermarket's return to high single-digit growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the aftermarket recovery follows strategy and go-to-market corrections, and expects sustained growth from a stronger portfolio and expanding workshop programme; no numbers given.

qa_highlights.question: Are the ~14% EBITDA margins sticky, and were there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited operational excellence, localisation, volume, productivity and favourable mix as sustained drivers; confirmed no one-offs in employee or other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Will the share of sourcing from parent fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise reflects volume surge; localisation plans are on track and will be updated in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Chassis acquisition accretive and what are the synergies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said synergies are minimal, it is a profitable company with good projects for several years, and consolidated results start next quarter; FY26 sales breakup to follow.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is from exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are at about 8-8.5% of revenue and the aim is to keep increasing this share over the next couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Is product mix favourable through FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, the product mix is quite favourable through the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the TACO and TSF JVs?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are in final stages of merger control clearance; the e-axles JV is expected to generate revenue by late next year, and order details to follow in about a quarter.

risks_watch: Commodity and currency volatility, geopolitical tensions in West Asia, and supply chain or logistics disruption remain open risks; management declined to guide on commodities.
Monsoon variability, potential El Nino and geopolitical tension are named as 2-wheeler demand downside risks.
Post-GST demand normalisation could arrive in one or two quarters, according to management.
Sourcing from the parent rising to about 53% of purchased goods; localisation progress to be tracked.
Timing of JV merger clearances and of CAFE Phase 3 and CV ADAS content opportunities; the CAFE content value was not disclosed.
Chassis Systems FY26 numbers and segment breakup not yet disclosed; consolidated impact to be assessed from next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, margins and the aftermarket turnaround, describing the quarter as exceptionally good. Cautious and deflecting on commodities, the timing of JV revenue, CAFE content value and Chassis synergies, saying these will be shared later. The CFO was on the call for the first time and said he was unwell, so Guruprasad Mudlapur answered most questions.
key_quotes: We've had a good quarter, exceptionally good quarter.
So we believe that this is a sustainable path over the coming period.

adds.what: Chassis Systems business acquired from Bosch sister company (completed July 2026); consolidation starts this quarter
JV with TACO (e-axles) to operate out of Nashik; revenue expected by late next year, awaiting merger control clearance
JV with TSF Group (air systems) to operate out of Chennai, awaiting merger control clearance

growth.why: Management gave a resilient 8% 2-wheeler industry growth outlook for next quarter and said margin upward trend and favourable mix will be sustained, but gave no numeric company revenue guidance; Q1 revenue grew 22% YoY, backed by Power Solutions volume and new launches, with the Chassis acquisition consolidating from this quarter and JVs still awaiting clearances.
